explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says that a nontrivial additive character ψ on the adic completion has an exact "level" ℓ: ψ is trivial on the ball of radius exp ℓ, but not on the ball of radius exp (ℓ+1). The proof finds this ℓ with a hand-written argument by induction over the integers. I grepped Mathlib for additive characters together with valuations or conductors (AddChar with Valued, conductor with AddChar) and found nothing. A generic lemma about integers that are greatest, or bounded above (e.g. Int.exists_greatest_of_bdd), only supplies part of the argument. Getting from it to this statement would still take several steps: showing that ψ is nontrivial somewhere, bounding the level, and so on. That is more than a short derivation.
